newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SME LOBBY CALLS FOR 2-YR LOW-COST PAY DEAL.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SME LOBBY CALLS FOR 2-YR LOW-COST PAY DEAL.

text.p: Finland's lobby of small- and medium-sized firms, the Federation of Finnish Enterprises, on Wednesday called for a two-year pay deal that would not raise total labour costs in the upcoming round of wage talks.

"The incomes policy settlement would be a two-year deal and general pay increases would be less than one percent per year," the federation said in a statement listing its objectives for the next collective bargaining round.
The federation has 75,000 medium-sized companies as its members. The current collective pay deal runs to end January 1998: the next bargaining round begins in earnest in autumn.
An income tax cut should be linked to a "moderate" incomes policy agreement, the federation said.
It called for a deal that would improve the growth and employment prospects of small firms.
